title: 2027 Hyundai Santa Cruz Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The 2027 Hyundai Santa Cruz gets a subtle update for the new model year, with a slimmed-down lineup featuring more standard equipment.
body_markdown:
Hyundai offers something for most buyers, with models ranging from the affordable Venue crossover to the luxurious three-row Palisade SUV. With the Santa Cruz, that includes those in the market for a compact pickup truck. Built on the same platform as the Tucson crossover SUV, the Santa Cruz is a unibody truck that competes directly with the Ford Maverick and, to a lesser degree, with the Honda Ridgeline and the all-electric Slate Truck.

## What’s New for the 2027 Hyundai Santa Cruz


Visually, there's little to separate the 2026 and the 2027 Santa Cruz. One thing buyers won't see on any 2027 model is a set of 20-inch wheels; they were standard on the previous Limited trim, which is no longer available. That change also means fingerprint recognition and genuine leather upholstery are gone for 2027, but the XRT now includes other Limited features. These include a Bose audio system, a heated steering wheel, an auto-dimming rearview mirror, and a rear armrest with integrated cupholders. Hyundai's H-Tex leatherette seats are now standard on all versions, and a power sunroof comes with all but the base model. Like the Limited, the Santa Cruz SEL has been discontinued, leaving the 2027 model with SE, SEL Activity, and XRT trims.


## Design


Beyond their underpinnings, the 2027 Santa Cruz and 2026 Tucson (the 2027 Tucson is all-new) share styling cues, from the arrangement of their LED headlights and daytime running lights to the power-dome hood and sleek roofline. Being a pickup truck, the Santa Cruz swaps the Tucson's enclosed cargo area for a four-foot composite bed with built-in underfloor storage and anchored tie-downs. Utility tracks and a tonneau cover are available. Beneath the tailgate is a bumper with integrated steps. All trims ride on 18-inch alloy wheels, though the XRT offers a distinct design and standard all-terrain tires. Every Santa Cruz has lower black cladding, but the SEL adds black roof rails and a sliding rear window, while the XRT sports a unique grille design, red tow hooks, bits of gray trim, and additional cladding above the side rocker panels. Hyundai claims the XRT offers an improved approach angle for better maneuverability off-road.


## Powertrain


All 2027 Hyundai Santa Cruz models come with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an eight-speed automatic transmission, but output varies by trim level. SE and SEL Activity models deliver 191 horsepower and 181 pound-feet of torque, with standard front-wheel drive (FWD) and available all-wheel drive (AWD). According to the EPA, drivers can expect to see 22 mpg city, 30 mpg highway, and 25 mpg combined in FWD guise, or 21 mpg, 29 mpg, and 24 mpg with the AWD system. This engine has a maximum towing capacity of 3,500 pounds. The Santa Cruz XRT has more punch, with 281 hp and 311 lb-ft of torque on tap. AWD is standard, as are paddle shifters, multiple terrain settings, and a tow mode. EPA-estimated fuel economy is 18 mpg city, 25 mpg highway, and 20 mpg combined. The added power ups towing capacity to 5,000 pounds.


## Interior


Inside, the five-passenger Santa Cruz strongly resembles the 2026 Tucson, with sweeping horizontal lines running from the door panels to the uncluttered dash top. Unlike the Tucson, the Santa Cruz features a traditional gearshift lever in the center console. All trims now come with leatherette upholstery, though a power driver's seat and heated front seats are reserved for the upper two trims, and the XRT gets embossed lettering. The Santa Cruz offers decent storage, with door cubbies, a center armrest console, and a removable bin under the rear seat. The XRT adds a fold-down rear armrest with cupholders, but no configuration improves rear legroom, which, for reference, is about 5 inches less than the Tucson.


## Technology


An expansive screen spans the area behind the steering wheel to the center dash and includes a 12.3-inch infotainment display and a 4.2-inch (SE) or 12.3-inch (SEL Activity, XRT) digital gauge display. The standard audio system includes six speakers, HD radio, and a trial SiriusXM satellite radio subscription, while the XRT gets a Bose audio system. All trim levels include wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, Hyundai's Bluelink+ connected services, and multiple USB ports. Starting with the SEL Activity, buyers get dual-zone automatic climate control and a wireless charger, but navigation, voice recognition, a heated steering wheel, and an auto-dimming rearview mirror require the XRT trim.

## Safety


For a relatively small vehicle, the 2027 Hyundai Santa Cruz packs in an impressive amount of safety equipment. Highlights include blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, forward-collision warning, lane-keep assist, lane-following assist, a driver-attention monitor, and safe-exit assist. Those items are standard on the SE and above, but the automaker takes things up a notch with the XRT's surround-view camera, navigation-based adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go, forward-collision warning with pedestrian and cyclist detection, and other components included in the Hyundai Driving Assist I suite of safety features. In National Highway Traffic Safety Administration tests, the 2027 Santa Cruz pickup earned the highest possible five-star overall rating. Results from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety were more mixed, with a Good score in the updated moderate overlap front test, a next-to-lowest Marginal rating for the responsiveness of the forward-collision warning and automatic emergency braking systems, and a more favorable Acceptable rating in most other categories.


## Pricing and Release Date


The 2027 Hyundai Santa Cruz is on sale now and, at the time of writing, the base SE FWD started at $30,300 plus a $1,650 destination charge. SEL Activity pricing starts at $34,700, and buyers can tack on AWD for $1,500. The XRT, standard with AWD, starts at $42,775. Hyundai doesn't offer any option packages, but there are several accessories, such as a $20 coin cup to a $755 set of side steps.
